title: Hollywood's biggest directors are pushing back against AI. Here's why.
excerpt: Christopher Nolan called AI "a Trojan horse that everybody knows the Greeks are inside." Guillermo del Toro said it could prevent future filmmakers from mastering their craft.
content_html:
Top movie directors are rejecting AI. Here's what they're worried about.

By Amanda Goh

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

As AI races ahead, Hollywood's top directors are trying to protect the craft behind great films.

Generative AI can now produce everything from scripts to visual effects, but some of cinema's most celebrated filmmakers argue it can't replicate the lived experience, creative judgment, and years of craftsmanship that make great art.

It's part of a wider reckoning over AI in Hollywood, where celebrities such as Taylor Swift and Matthew McConaughey have also sought to protect their likeness from AI-generated impersonations.

Here's what some of cinema's biggest creative voices have to say about AI.

Guillermo del Toro says AI could deprive the next generation of learning how to make films

Guillermo del Toro said AI could prevent future filmmakers from mastering their craft.

At the 2026 San Diego Comic Con, which ran from Thursday through Sunday, the Mexican director said the 3D rerelease of "Pan's Labyrinth" was created through a manual conversion process.

"Obviously, I said, 'Absolutely no goddamn AI,'" del Toro said.

He said he didn't mind the added cost of the manual approach, which involved about 1,000 artists rotoscoping the film.

"What we're protecting is the beauty and the redeeming power of art. It's not about who gets the job. We are protecting a lineage of art. If we cut a generation of people from learning their craft, you're cutting the rest of the history of that medium away from them, for what?" del Toro said.

Rather than opting for the fastest approach, del Toro said he prioritized quality.

"You have to put in time. You roto every element by hand. A human-made decision of depth," he said.

Christopher Nolan says AI should be viewed with skepticism

Christopher Nolan said people should be just as skeptical of AI's creators as they are of the technology itself.

In a July 14 conversation with YouTuber HugoDécrypte, Nolan called AI "a Trojan horse that everybody knows the Greeks are inside."

"I've never seen a technology advancing so rapidly, so completely rejected by the public," Nolan said.

He added that he has been struck by the level of public skepticism toward AI, particularly among the younger generation, who have popularized the term "AI slop."

Nolan said he welcomed that skepticism, arguing that while technology can bring "great gifts," it should always be approached with caution.

"The motives of the people giving it to us also have to be viewed with skepticism. That's when we'll get the best out of a new technology, rather than just blind faith that everything's going to be great," Nolan said.

Nolan is known for favoring real stunt work, practical effects, and in-camera techniques over extensive CGI. His latest film, "The Odyssey," follows that tradition and has grossed over $639 million worldwide since its July 17 release, per Box Office Mojo.

Steven Spielberg says AI shouldn't take the place of creative people

Steven Spielberg said he draws the line at using AI to replace human creativity.

"I have never used AI on any of my films yet," the filmmaker said at the 2026 SXSW conference, which was held in Austin in March.

"Even television, we have a writer's room. All the seats are occupied. There's not an empty chair with a laptop in front of it," Spielberg said. "I haven't used AI that way."

The filmmaker added that he isn't completely against the technology, saying he is "for AI in many different disciplines."

"I am not for AI that replaces a creative individual," Spielberg said.

Tim Burton says AI strips away the humanity behind art

Tim Burton said seeing AI-generated artwork in his signature style left him deeply unsettled.

In 2023, Burton shared his thoughts on BuzzFeed using AI to create Disney characters in his distinctive style.

"I can't describe the feeling it gives you. It reminded me of when other cultures say, 'Don't take my picture because it is taking away your soul," Burton told The Independent.

Even though Burton said some of the AI-generated pieces were "very good," he found it unsettling to see a machine recreate his visual style.

"It's like a robot taking your humanity, your soul," he said.

Bong Joon Ho says AI is forcing people to rethink what only humans can create

Bong Joon Ho, the Oscar-winning director of "Parasite," has a tongue-in-cheek solution for AI: wipe it out.

"My official answer is, AI is good because it's the very beginning of the human race finally seriously thinking about what only humans can do. But my personal answer is, I'm going to organize a military squad, and their mission is to destroy AI," Bong said at the 2025 Marrakech Film Festival, per Deadline.

Celine Song says AI risks erasing the struggles that make life beautiful

Celine Song said artists have a responsibility to defend what makes us human.

Speaking at the 2025 Marrakech Film Festival, per Deadline, the "Past Lives" director said she is "very concerned" about the way AI is "trying to encroach" on the experiences that make life both beautiful and worthwhile.

"The number one thing that we're here to defend as artists is humanity," Song said. "We're here not to think about what makes human life easy, what makes it convenient, but what it's like to actually live."

content_html_zh:
顶级电影导演正在拒绝人工智能。 这就是他们担心的事情。

作者：Amanda Goh 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

随着人工智能的发展，好莱坞的顶级导演正在努力保护伟大电影背后的工艺。

生成式人工智能现在可以制作从剧本到视觉效果的一切内容，但一些最著名的电影制作人认为，它无法复制创造伟大艺术的生活经验、创造性判断和多年的工艺。

这是好莱坞对人工智能更广泛反思的一部分，泰勒·斯威夫特和马修·麦康纳等名人也试图保护自己的形象免受人工智能生成的模仿。

以下是一些电影界最具创意的人士对人工智能的看法。

吉列尔莫·德尔·托罗表示人工智能可能会剥夺下一代学习如何制作电影的机会

吉列尔莫·德尔·托罗表示，人工智能可能会阻碍未来的电影制作人掌握他们的技艺。

在周四至周日举行的 2026 年圣地亚哥动漫展上，这位墨西哥导演表示，《潘神的迷宫》的 3D 重新发布是通过手动转换过程创建的。

“显然，我说，‘绝对没有该死的人工智能，’”德尔托罗说。

他表示，他并不介意手动方法的额外成本，该方法涉及大约 1,000 名艺术家对影片进行动态描画。

“我们保护的是艺术的美丽和救赎力量。 这不是谁得到这份工作的问题。 我们正在保护艺术的传承。 如果我们阻止一代人学习他们的手艺，那么你就将这种媒体的其余历史从他们手中夺走，为了什么？” 德尔·托罗说道。

德尔托罗表示，他并没有选择最快的方法，而是优先考虑质量。

“你必须投入时间。 您手动旋转每个元素。 这是人为的深度决定，”他说。

克里斯托弗·诺兰表示应该以怀疑的态度看待人工智能

克里斯托弗·诺兰表示，人们应该对人工智能的创造者持怀疑态度，就像对技术本身持怀疑态度一样。

在 7 月 14 日与 YouTuber HugoDécrypte 的对话中，诺兰称人工智能是“众所周知的特洛伊木马，里面藏着希腊人”。

诺兰说：“我从未见过一项技术进步得如此之快，以至于被公众彻底拒绝。”

他补充说，公众对人工智能的怀疑程度让他感到震惊，尤其是年轻一代，他们普及了“AI slop”这个词。

诺兰表示，他欢迎这种怀疑，并认为虽然技术可以带来“伟大的礼物”，但应该始终谨慎对待。

“人们向我们提供这些信息的动机也必须持怀疑态度。 那时我们将充分利用新技术，而不是盲目地相信一切都会很棒，”诺兰说。

诺兰以偏爱真实的特技、实际效果和镜头内技术而不是广泛的 CGI 而闻名。 他的最新电影《奥德赛》遵循了这一传统，根据 Box Office Mojo 的数据，自 7 月 17 日上映以来，全球票房已超过 6.39 亿美元。

史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格表示人工智能不应该取代有创造力的人

史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格表示，他在使用人工智能取代人类创造力方面划清了界限。

这位电影制片人在 3 月份于奥斯汀举行的 2026 年 SXSW 会议上表示：“我从未在我的任何电影中使用过人工智能。”

“即使是电视，我们也有作家室。 所有座位都被占满了。 没有一张空椅子，前面放着一台笔记本电脑，”斯皮尔伯格说。 “我没有这样使用过人工智能。”

这位电影制片人补充说，他并不完全反对这项技术，并表示他“支持许多不同学科的人工智能”。

斯皮尔伯格说：“我不赞成人工智能取代有创造力的个人。”

蒂姆·伯顿表示人工智能剥夺了艺术背后的人性

蒂姆·伯顿表示，看到人工智能生成的具有他标志性风格的艺术作品让他深感不安。

2023 年，Burton 分享了他对 BuzzFeed 使用人工智能以他独特的风格创造迪士尼角色的想法。

“我无法描述它给你的感觉。 这让我想起其他文化中的说法，‘不要拍我的照片，因为它会带走你的灵魂，’伯顿告诉《独立报》。

尽管伯顿说人工智能生成的一些作品“非常好”，但他发现看到机器重现他的视觉风格感到不安。

“这就像一个机器人夺走了你的人性、你的灵魂，”他说。

奉俊昊表示人工智能正在迫使人们重新思考只有人类才能创造的东西

《寄生虫》奥斯卡获奖导演奉俊昊对人工智能提出了一个半开玩笑的解决方案：消灭它。

“我的官方答案是，人工智能是好的，因为它是人类最终认真思考只有人类才能做的事情的开始。 但我个人的答案是，我将组织一支军队，他们的任务是摧毁人工智能，”奉俊昊在 2025 年马拉喀什电影节上说道。

Celine Song 表示人工智能有可能消除让生活变得美好的挣扎

席琳·宋 (Celine Song) 表示，艺术家有责任捍卫我们人类的本质。

这位《前世今生》导演在 2025 年马拉喀什电影节上发表讲话时表示，她“非常担心”人工智能“试图侵占”让生活变得美好和有价值的体验。

“作为艺术家，我们要捍卫的第一件事就是人性，”宋说。 “我们来这里不是为了思考什么让人类的生活变得轻松、方便，而是真正生活的感觉如何。”
